   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><b><i>Indemnification</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company has entered into indemnification agreements with its directors and executive officers. These agreements, among other things, require AvePoint to indemnify its directors and executive officers to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law, specifically the Delaware General Corporation Law (as the same exists or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>hereafter be amended) for certain expenses, including attorneys&#8217; fees, judgments, fines, and settlement amounts incurred by a director or executive officer in any action or proceeding arising out of their services as&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;of the Company&#8217;s directors or executive officers or any other company or enterprise to which the person provides services at the Company&#8217;s request.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As part of the business combination with Apex Technology Acquisition Corporation (&#8220;<b><i>Apex</i></b>&#8221;), we assumed certain indemnification obligations for Apex Technology Sponsor LLC and Jeff Epstein, Brad Koenig, David Chao, Peter Bell, Donna Wells, and Alex Vieux (the &#8220;<b><i>Indemnitees</i></b>&#8221; or &#8220;<b><i>Defendants</i></b>&#8221;). On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2, 2024,&#160;</em>Drulias and Farzad (as purported Apex stockholders, the &#8220;<b><i>Plaintiffs</i></b>&#8221;) filed a class action complaint against the Indemnities in Delaware Court of Chancery, captioned Dean William Drulias, et.al. v. Apex Technology Sponsor LLC, et.al., C.A.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No.</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">0094</em>-LWW. Plaintiffs asserted breach of fiduciary duty and unjust enrichment claims against the Defendants. The complaint alleged that Defendants made false and misleading disclosures in the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 2, 2021&#160;</em>proxy statement of Apex impacting its stockholders&#8217; vote to approve a merger between Apex and us and also affecting stockholders&#8217; redemption rights prior to the merger. Plaintiffs sought unspecified damages, rescission or rescissory damages, and disgorgement of unjust enrichment. We were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;a named defendant in the complaint but had indemnification obligations to the Defendants under indemnification agreements executed during the merger. Also, in accordance with the business combination agreement, the Defendants obtained insurance policies to cover post-closing liability, with Apex securing a policy with a limit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622496" contextRef="d_2024-02-02_2024-02-02_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-DefendantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:InsurancePolicyPostclosingLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and the sponsors obtaining a policy with a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622497" contextRef="d_2024-02-02_2024-02-02_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-SponsorsMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:InsurancePolicyPostclosingLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million limit. The parties participated in a mediation in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 2024 </em>and agreed to settlement terms. Pursuant to a fully executed&#160;settlement agreement, releasing us and the Defendants and settling the class action, we contributed $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622498" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsForLegalSettlements" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter toward the full settlement amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622500" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2024-10-31_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedToOtherParty" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">14.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The remaining $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622501" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2024-10-31_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:LitigationCaseRemainingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">13</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was&#160;paid pursuant to the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;aforementioned insurance policies covering the Defendants and sponsor. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em>&#160;an estimated accrual of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622504" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-AccruedExpenseAndOtherCurrentLiabilitiesMember_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622505" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-AccruedExpenseAndOtherCurrentLiabilitiesMember_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, was included in the accrued expenses and other current liabilities within the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> Company Earn-Out and Warrant Liabilities</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><i><b>Company Earn-Out</b></i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain holders of&#160;common stock and certain holders of options shall be issued additional shares of AvePoint&#8217;s common stock, as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 8pt;">&#9632;</td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 0pt;"><ix:nonFraction id="c140622511" contextRef="d_2021-07-26_2021-07-26" unitRef="Share" name="avpt:NumberOfSharesExchangeableAt1250" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of AvePoint&#8217;s common stock, in the aggregate, if at any time from <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021 </em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028 (</em>a)&#160;AvePoint&#8217;s&#160;stock price is greater than or equal to <em style="font: inherit;">$12.50</em> over any <em style="font: inherit;">20</em> Trading Days within any <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> trading day period or (b)&#160;the Company consummates a subsequent transaction, which results in the stockholders of the Company having the right to exchange their shares for cash, securities or other property having a value equaling or exceeding <em style="font: inherit;">$12.50</em> per share;</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 8pt;">&#9632;</td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 0pt;"><ix:nonFraction id="c140622516" contextRef="d_2021-07-26_2021-07-26" unitRef="Share" name="avpt:NumberOfSharesExchangeableAt1500" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of AvePoint&#8217;s common stock, in the aggregate, if at any time from <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021 </em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028&#160;(</em>a)&#160;AvePoint&#8217;s&#160;stock price is greater than or equal to <em style="font: inherit;">$15.00</em> over any <em style="font: inherit;">20</em> Trading Days within any <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> trading day period or (b)&#160;the Company consummates a subsequent transaction, which results in the stockholders of the Company having the right to exchange their shares for cash, securities or other property having a value equaling or exceeding <em style="font: inherit;">$15.00</em> per share;</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 8pt;">&#9632;</td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 0pt;"><ix:nonFraction id="c140622521" contextRef="d_2021-07-26_2021-07-26" unitRef="Share" name="avpt:NumberOfSharesExchangeableAt1750" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of AvePoint&#8217;s common stock, in the aggregate, if at any time from <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021 </em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028 (</em>a)&#160;AvePoint&#8217;s&#160;stock price is greater than or equal to <em style="font: inherit;">$17.50</em> over any <em style="font: inherit;">20</em> Trading Days within any <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> trading day period or (b)&#160;the Company consummates a subsequent transaction, which results in the stockholders of the Company having the right to exchange their shares for cash, securities or other property having a value equaling or exceeding <em style="font: inherit;">$17.50</em> per share.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The rights described above are hereafter referred to as the &#8220;<i><b>Company Earn-Out Shares</b></i>&#8221;. To the extent that any portion of the Company Earn-Out Shares that would otherwise be issued to a holder of options that remain&#160;unvested at the date of the milestones described above, then in lieu of issuing the applicable Company Earn-Out Shares, the Company shall instead issue an award of restricted stock units of the Company for a number of shares of AvePoint&#8217;s common stock equal to such portion of the Company Earn-Out Shares issuable with respect to the unvested options (the &#8220;<i><b>Company Earn-Out RSUs</b></i>&#8221;). In evaluation of the Company Earn-Out Shares and Company Earn-Out RSUs, management determined that the Company Earn-Out Shares represent derivatives to be marked to market at each reporting period, while the Company Earn-Out RSUs represent&#160;equity. Refer to&#160;&#8220;<i>Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;&#8212; Stock-Based Compensation</i>&#8221; for more information regarding the Company Earn-Out RSUs.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">In order to capture the market conditions associated with the Company Earn-Out&#160;Shares, the Company applied an approach that incorporated a Monte Carlo simulation, which involved random iterations that took different future price paths over the Sponsor Earn-Out Shares&#8217; contractual life based on the appropriate probability distributions. The fair value was determined by taking the average of the fair values under each Monte Carlo simulation trial. The Monte Carlo model requires highly subjective assumptions including the expected volatility of the price of our common stock, and the expected term of the earn-out shares. Significant increases or decreases to these inputs in isolation could result in a significantly higher or lower liability. Under this approach, the fair value of the&#160;Company Earn-Out&#160;Shares on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021, </em>was determined to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622527" contextRef="i_2021-07-01" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationContingentConsiderationLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">29.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

Consequently, the fair value of the private placement warrants is equivalent to the quoted price of the publicly traded warrants<i>.</i>&#160;Under this approach, the fair value of the&#160;private placement warrants on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021, </em>was determined to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622540" contextRef="i_2021-07-01_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:WarrantsAndRightsOutstanding" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. As a result, the public warrants were reclassified from other liabilities to additional paid-in capital in the consolidated balance sheets. Following the reclassification,&#160;there were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;remaining private placement warrants. The fair value was remeasured as of the Private Warrants Transfer Date&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>and was determined to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622542" contextRef="i_2025-04-10_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:WarrantsAndRightsOutstanding" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622543" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:WarrantsAndRightsOutstanding" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, and included in other&#160;liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Share Repurchase Program</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 17, 2022, </em>the Company announced that its Board of Directors authorized a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622567">three</span>-year&#160;share repurchase program (the &#8220;<b><i>Share Repurchase Program</i></b>&#8221;), which was renewed for an additional <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 25, 2025.&#160;</em>Under the Share Repurchase Program, the Company has the authority to buy up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622569" contextRef="i_2022-02-25" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction> million of common stock&#160;via acquisitions in the open market or privately negotiated transactions. The Share Repurchase Program&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be suspended or discontinued at any time. The Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligated to make purchases of, nor is it obligated to acquire any particular amount of, common stock under the Share Repurchase Program. As a result of the exercise, AvePoint&#8217;s ownership in MaivenPoint was <ix:nonFraction id="c140622622" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_OwnershipAxis-AvepointEdutechPteLtdMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">76.1</ix:nonFraction>%, with the remaining ownership interest held by AEPL as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024. </em>Due to the exercise of the put option, the Company adjusted the carrying amount of the noncontrolling interest by multiplying the adjusted net assets of MaivenPoint AEPL&#8217;s new ownership percentage, resulting in a reduction to noncontrolling interest and increase in additional paid-in capital of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622623" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-AdditionalPaidInCapitalMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestDecreaseFromRedemptions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">6.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, within the consolidated balance sheets.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">There were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em> put options held by MaivenPoint&#8217;s remaining noncontrolling interest shareholders, and therefore, there was <ix:nonFraction id="c140622625" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RedeemableNoncontrollingInterestEquityCarryingAmount" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> redeemable noncontrolling interest in MaivenPoint as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2025, </em>the Company repurchased all of the remaining outstanding interest of MaivenPoint from AEPL for an aggregate cash purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622626" contextRef="d_2025-05-30_2025-05-30_OwnershipAxis-AvepointEdutechPteLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireAdditionalInterestInSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.1</ix:nonFraction> million. Following the repurchase of the interest, the Company is the sole interest holder&#160;of MaivenPoint.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">15.</em> Growth Equity Fund</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2024,&#160;</em>the Company and Lumens Capital Partners Ltd. (&#8220;<b><i>LCP</i></b>&#8221;) established&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">A3V</em></i>&#160;JV Co. (the &#8220;<b><i>Venture</i></b>&#8221;), with each owning an equal share of the Venture.&#160;In addition, the Company entered into a separate agreement with LCP to form the Fund.&#160;The Fund is a Cayman Islands-exempted limited partnership, aimed at investing in companies in the growth equity phase and mature cashflow generating businesses with strong growth potential. The Fund looks to invest in companies situated in enterprise software markets aligning with the professional expertise and geographical presence of both the Company and LCP.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Venture wholly owns&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">A3V</em>&#160;GP Co., which serves&#160;as the general partner of the Fund. As a limited partner, the Company committed to contribute $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622630" contextRef="d_2024-02-28_2024-02-28_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityFinancialOrOtherSupportAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to the Fund, to be called as needed, for portfolio investments, fees, and expenses of the Fund. The Company also participates in Fund establishment costs and an annual management fee equal to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140622631" contextRef="i_2024-02-28_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="Pure" name="avpt:ManagementFeePercentOfTotalCommitment" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2.0</ix:nonFraction>% of the total commitment. Any future repayment obligations will be triggered upon the receipt by LCP of profit allocations related to the Fund.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the Company decided to discontinue its participation in the Fund. As a result, during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company recorded a credit loss of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622632" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-09-30_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProvisionForLoanLossesExpensed" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million, which was a non-cash investing activity, offset by a reduction of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622633" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-09-30_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:IncreaseDecreaseInVariableInterestEntityLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of accrued expenses. Both were included in general and administrative in the consolidated statements of income (loss). During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company also recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622634" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestReceivable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million interest loss included in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of income (loss).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;portion of the Company&#8217;s $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622636" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityFinancialOrOtherSupportAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million commitment has been called or was callable.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, an estimated payable of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622638" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeePayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622639" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-A3VenturesFund1LpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeePayable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, were&#160;included in accrued expenses and other current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><b><i>Stock Options </i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The compensation costs for stock option awards are recognized using the straight-line attribution method over the requite service period and are accounted for forfeitures as they occur. Stock options vest over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622651">four</span>-year service period and expire on the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622652">tenth</span> anniversary of the date of award.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><i><b>Restricted Stock Units</b></i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Under the terms of the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan, we have issued stock unit awards with a continuous employment condition only (&#8220;<b><i>Time-Based RSUs</i></b>&#8221;), and restricted stock unit&#160;awards with a continuous employment condition that are also contingent on the Company meeting certain performance goals (&#8220;<b><i>PSUs</i></b>&#8221;, and together &#8220;<b><i>RSUs</i></b>&#8221;). Both types of RSU awards vest over a&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622678">four</span>-year period from the grant date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The compensation costs for RSUs are recognized using the straight-line attribution method over the requisite service period and are accounted for forfeitures as they occur. RSUs are&#160;measured at the fair market value of the underlying stock at the grant date.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The total fair value of shares vested during the years ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, &#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622688" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsVestedInPeriodTotalFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">75.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622689" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsVestedInPeriodTotalFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">51.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622690" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsVestedInPeriodTotalFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">18.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;there was $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622691" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedShareBasedAwardsOtherThanOptions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">54.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in unrecognized compensation costs specific to the non-vested RSUs under the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan. This unrecognized stock-based compensation cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of approximately <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" id="c140622693" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2.5</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><i><b>Company Earn-Out RSUs</b></i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The compensation costs for Company Earn-Out RSUs&#160;are recognized using the straight-line attribution method over the requite service period and are accounted for forfeitures as they occur. In order to capture the market conditions associated with the Company Earn-Out&#160;RSUs, the Company applied an approach that incorporated a Monte Carlo simulation, which involved random iterations that took different future price paths over the Sponsor Earn-Out RSUs&#8217; contractual life based on the appropriate probability distributions. The fair value was determined by taking the average of the fair values under each Monte Carlo simulation trial. Under this approach, the grant-date fair value of the&#160;Company Earn-Out&#160;RSUs on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2021, </em>was determined to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622694" contextRef="i_2021-07-21_AwardTypeAxis-EarnOutRSUsMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsOutstandingFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The stock options underlying the Earn-Out RSUs vest&#160;over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622695">four</span>-year period and expire on the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622696">tenth</span> anniversary of the date of award.&#160;If the contingent milestones of the&#160;Earn-Out RSUs are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met by <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2028, </em>the holders of the underlying stock options will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> receive the Earn-Out RSUs. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>all Company Earn-Out RSUs are fully vested. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> the Company recorded stock-based compensation expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622701" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EarnOutRSUsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622702" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EarnOutRSUsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, related to these Earn-Out RSUs.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">17.</em> Fair Value Measurements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Fair value is the price that would be received upon selling an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Assets and liabilities recorded at fair value are measured and classified in accordance with a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-level fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy requires entities to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs. The <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels of inputs used to measure fair value are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 8pt;">&#9632;</td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8212;&#160;Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the reporting entity can access at the measurement date.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-size: 8pt;">&#9632;</td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8212;&#160;Inputs other than quoted prices included within Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1</em> that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0pt; margin: 3pt 0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 3pt 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8212;&#160;Unobservable inputs for the asset or liability.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)</sup> The majority of certificates of deposit are foreign deposits.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">(<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;</sup>The fair value of mandatorily redeemable noncontrolling interest is based on discounted redemption value using risk-free rates offered for similar financing with the same remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">(<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;</sup>During&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em>&#160;the Company extended a credit facility to LCP with a total commitment of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622716" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-LumensCapitalPartnersLtdTheLcpMember" unitRef="USD" name="avpt:NotesReceivableMaximumCommitment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and maturities of greater than&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>&#160;months (the &#8220;<b><i>LCP Notes Receivable</i></b>&#8221;). Refer to &#8220;<i>Note</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">15</em></i>&#160;<i>-&#160;</i><i>Growth Equity Fund</i>&#8221; for further details. The LCP Notes Receivable bear interest at an annual rate equal to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c140622719" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-LumensCapitalPartnersLtdTheLcpMember" unitRef="Pure" name="avpt:NotesReceivableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">8</ix:nonFraction>%.&#160; As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the LCP Notes Receivable in the amounts of $<ix:nonFraction id="c140622720" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-LumensCapitalPartnersLtdTheLcpMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was included in other assets within the consolidated balance sheets. Fair value is based on discounted future cash flows using current interest rates offered for similar notes to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;parties with similar credit ratings for the same remaining maturities.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">18.</em> Segment Information </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company manages its business activities on a consolidated basis and operates&#160;in a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622873"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c140622874">single</span></span> operating segment. Its products and services are sold throughout the world, through direct and indirect sales channels. The Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker (the &#8220;<b><i>CODM</i></b>&#8221;) is the Chief Executive Officer. The CODM makes operating performance assessment and resource allocation decisions on a consolidated basis. The CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> review&#160;assets in evaluating the results of the segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM assesses performance for the consolidated entity and decides how to allocate resources based on net income (loss) reported on the consolidated statements of income (loss). The CODM uses net income (loss)&#160;to monitor budgeted versus actual results and to conduct competitive analysis by benchmarking against industry peers. Additionally, net income (loss) serves as a basis for making strategic decisions, such as acquisitions and reinvestments into business, and establishing management compensation linked to segment performance.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" id="c3113417" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">20.</em> Net Income (Loss) Per Share </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Basic net income (loss) per share&#160;is computed by dividing total net income (loss) by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period. In computing diluted net income (loss), the Company adjusts the denominator, subject to anti-dilution requirements, to include the dilution from potential shares of common stock resulting from outstanding share-based payment awards, warrants, and Company Earn-Outs. The Company applies&#160;the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method in calculating loss per share. The Company&#8217;s Sponsor Earn-Out Shares&#160;described in &#8220;<i>Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em>&#160;&#8212; Mezzanine Equity and Stockholders&#8217;</i><i>&#160;Equity</i>&#8221; are considered participating securities and have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> contractual obligation to shares in the loss of the Company. As such, the weighted-average impact of these shares is excluded from the calculation of loss per share below.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
     The Company has entered into indemnification agreements with its directors and executive officers. These agreements,&#160;among other things,&#160;require AvePoint to indemnify its directors and executive officers to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law,&#160;specifically the Delaware General Corporation Law (as the same exists or
    <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>hereafter be amended) for certain expenses, including attorneys&#8217; fees, judgments, fines, and settlement amounts incurred by a director or executive officer in any action or proceeding arising out of their services as
    <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the Company&#8217;s directors or executive officers or any other company or enterprise to which the person provides services at the Company&#8217;s request.

  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;"><b><a id="item9" title="item9" href="#"></a>ITEM 9.&#160;CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</b></p>

   &#160;

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="item9a" title="item9a" href="#"></a>ITEM 9A.&#160;CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (in his capacity as &#8220;<i><b>Principal Executive Officer</b></i>&#8221;) and our Chief Financial Officer (in his capacity as&#160;&#8220;<i><b>Principal Financial and Accounting Officer</b></i>&#8221;), we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and&#160;15d-15(e)) under the Exchange Act, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report. Based upon that evaluation, our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial and Accounting Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were&#160;effective as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Management</span></i></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#8217;</span><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) of the Exchange Act. Our system of internal control was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes, in accordance with GAAP. Management conducted an assessment of the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on the criteria set forth in Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (the &#8220;<i><b>COSO&#160;framework</b></i>&#8221;). Based on management&#8217;s assessment, our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial and Accounting Officer concluded that our&#160;internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2025&#160;to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP.&#160; Our independent registered public accounting firm, Deloitte &amp; Touch LLP, has issued an audit report with respect to our internal control over financial reporting, which appears in Part II, Item 9A&#160;in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</span></i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">There have not been any&#160;changes in the Company&#8217;s&#160;internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act)&#160;during the fourth quarter&#160;ended December 31, 2025, that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s&#160;internal control over financial reporting.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: center;"><b>PART II</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: center;"><b>Items 9A</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: center;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><span style="text-transform:uppercase;"><b>Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">To the stockholders and the Board of Directors of AvePoint, Inc.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Opinion on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of AvePoint, Inc. and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of December 31, 2025, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control </i>&#8212;<i> Integrated Framework (2013)</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, based on criteria established in <i>Internal Control </i>&#8212;<i> Integrated Framework (2013)</i> issued by COSO.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), consolidated financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025, of the Company and our report dated February 26, 2026, expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Basis for Opinion</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Definition and Limitations of Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
